summary: Expiry Countdown Timer feature fully tested and working. All 14 backend tests pass. Frontend UI verified: Admin Users list shows Timer column, Admin Create User has timer input in Step 4, Admin Edit User has Expiry Countdown Timer card in Actions tab, WalletDashboard shows live countdown when fees are blocked.
critical_code_review_comments: Fixed bug in server.py: admin_create_user was returning user.model_dump() which didn't include timer_duration_hours. Changed to return user_dict_for_response which includes the timer field.
seed_data_creation: Created test user with timer_duration_hours=48 and €150 unpaid fees for testing countdown feature
context_for_next_testing_agent: Expiry Countdown Timer feature is fully implemented and tested. Test user 'Timer Test' has active timer showing ~48h countdown. The timer starts automatically when user opens withdraw modal with fees blocked.

backend: POST /api/wallet/start-timer - starts timer if timer_duration_hours is set
POST /api/wallet/start-timer - returns 'no_timer_configured' if no timer set
POST /api/wallet/start-timer - returns 'already_started' if timer already running
PUT /api/admin/users/{user_id} - accepts timer_duration_hours and timer_started_at fields
GET /api/admin/users - returns timer fields in user list
frontend: Admin Users list has 'Timer' column showing status (-, Not started, remaining time)
Admin Create User page has 'Expiry Timer (Hours)' input in Step 4
Admin Edit User page has 'Expiry Countdown Timer' card in Actions tab
WalletDashboard withdraw modal shows live countdown (47h 59m 58s format)
Timer starts automatically via API when user opens withdraw modal with fees blocked

bug_fixed.description: admin_create_user endpoint was not returning timer_duration_hours in response
bug_fixed.root_cause: user.model_dump() was called on the User model object before timer_duration_hours was added to user_dict
bug_fixed.fix: Changed to return user_dict_for_response which includes the timer field after it's added
